chapter_seo_title: The Creditor of Blades: Li Huowang Meets Hong Da in the Supervisory Heavenly Office
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang tracks down a member of the Supervisory Heavenly Office, only to find a “Creditor of Blades” who kills innocents to sell a rumor. The price of entry into this system may be steeper than a blade.
og_title: The Creditor of Blades: A New Face in the Heavenly Office
og_description: Li Huowang meets Hong Da, a rogue agent of the Supervisory Heavenly Office whose methods are as brutal as his reputation. A debt of rust may be the cost of entry.
twitter_title: Li Huowang Bargains with a Blade-Lender
twitter_description: The Supervisory Heavenly Office doesn't hire heroes. It loans out Creditors of Blades—and the interest is paid in blood.

lore_anchors.definition: A folkloric figure who would loan knives or scissors on credit, only collecting payment after an eerie prophecy came true. In this novel, the archetype is weaponized into an agent of the Supervisory Heavenly Office whose blades carry supernatural obligations.

A government-backed organization that polices rogue cultivators, supernatural disasters, and Heavenly Calamities in the Dao-Twisted World. Its agents are often half-folk specialists with unique folk-magic backgrounds rather than standardized immortals.

A bureaucratic title within the Ministry of Rites, responsible for registering the identities and likenesses of individuals. Refusing to visit him signals Li Huowang’s fear of entering a government stronghold where his secrets might be exposed.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Hong Da kill innocent people?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He needed a brutal, believable counter-rumor to the Zuowandao's lie about the life-root-stealing ghost. In the logic of the Supervisory Heavenly Office, the lives of a few commoners are an acceptable cost to break a Zuowandao narrative.
